[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:new pages]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:Completion tier 2]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

revision.text:
'''正四位'''（しょうしい）とは、[[日本]]の[[位階]]及び[[神階]]における位のひとつ。
[[従三位]]の下、[[従四位]]の上に位する。[[贈位]]の場合、贈正四位という。
== 概要 == ===官位相当制における正四位の位置付け=== 正四位は[[律令制]]下においては上下に分けられ、従三位の下、従四位の上に位する。[[勲等]]では、[[勲三等]]に相当し、[[官位相当]]では正四位上は[[中務省|中務卿]]、[[参議]]に相当し、正四位下は[[皇太子傅]]及び中務省を除く八省の[[長官]]である[[卿]]（[[式部省|式部卿]]、[[治部省|治部卿]]、[[民部省|民部卿]]、[[兵部省|兵部卿]]、[[刑部省|刑部卿]]、[[大蔵省 (律令制)|大蔵卿]]、[[宮内省 (律令制)|宮内卿]]）の職がこの位にあった。しかし、後代には正四位の位階は本来従三位相当である筈の[[近衛大将]]が大臣の兼官となることが慣例化するに連れて、従三位の者が[[近衛府|近衛中将]]に任ぜられ、三位中将となることが通例化すると、正四位の者は[[近衛府|近衛少将]]に任ぜられることが慣例化するようになった（[[結城秀康]]など）。但し、正四位上については従三位に昇進予定者が一時昇叙する特別な位階であり、[[官位相当制]]では正四位下が主に用いられた。尤も、江戸時代に入ると、[[彦根藩|彦根]][[藩主]]の[[井伊氏]]の極位が正四位上とされたこともあり、時代により位階の運用に差異があることは留意する必要がある。
=== 正四位の格式と主な叙位者 === 従四位同様、四位にある者の敬称は[[氏]]及び[[諱]]の下に、[[朝臣]]を付ける名乗りが基本である。例として「正四位下前[[伊予国|伊予守]][[源頼義]]朝臣」など。
しかし、正四位であっても[[参議]]となり、[[公卿]]に列した者への敬称は氏の下に「[[朝臣]]」、諱の下に「卿」と称した。 一方、正四位下は[[公卿]]に昇ることを許されない[[家柄]]の極位、即ち最高位であり、著名なところでは[[清和源氏]]とりわけ、[[摂津源氏]]、[[河内源氏]]の[[棟梁]]に多くみられた。[[清和源氏]]では初代 [[源経基|経基王]]その子の[[源満仲]]、また満仲の[[長男]] [[摂津源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼光]]、[[河内源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼義]]、[[源義家|義家]]親子など河内源氏代々の棟梁がその位階に昇った。また、[[摂津源氏]]の[[傍系]]ではある、[[美濃源氏]]の[[源光保]]は[[院近臣]]として活躍し、娘 [[土佐局]]が[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽法皇]]の寵妃となったことで正四位下に昇った。 一方、武家の棟梁として源氏と覇を競った[[平氏#桓武平氏|桓武平氏]]では、公家平氏を別として武家平氏については官位の面でも長らく源氏に遅れをとっていた。しかし、源義家の子 [[源義親|義親]]が[[九州]]や[[隠岐国]]で濫妨を働き、[[平正盛]]がこれを討伐したことで、平氏は家格を上昇させ、その子 [[平忠盛]]の代に正四位上[[刑部卿]]にまで昇り、その嫡男 [[平清盛|清盛]]も29歳の若さで正四位下中務大輔兼安芸守となり、[[平氏政権]]の礎を築いている。源氏においては、[[源頼朝|頼朝]]が平氏追討を遂げるまでの間、この位階に留まったほか、[[鎌倉時代]]は[[鎌倉幕府]][[執権]]北条氏の得宗及び有力一門や有が叙せられ、[[得宗]]では[[北条泰時]]が、有力一門では[[北条政村]]が叙せられた。そのほか、京都の学者貴族出身の有力御家人 [[大江広元]]もこの位階に叙せられている。
[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には飛騨の国司大名 [[姉小路氏]]や[[北畠氏]]が正四位ないし従三位に昇るなど公家大名に叙位例が見られる他、一国人領主ながら三管領斯波家の女を母とする、源氏の名門 [[村上義清]]が正四位上に昇っている。 [[江戸時代]]には、御三家の[[水戸藩]]の[[水戸徳川家]]の当主、家門大名では[[福井藩]]の[[越前松平家]]（15代中4人）、[[譜代大名]]では[[彦根藩]]の[[井伊氏]]（17代中3人）、[[外様大名]]の[[加賀藩]]の[[前田氏]]や[[薩摩藩]]の[[島津氏]]（12代中、[[島津斉宣]]のみ）、[[仙台藩]]の[[伊達氏]]（歴代では[[伊達慶邦]]のみ）などの大名家が昇ることを許された。
[[明治|明治時代]]以降、正四位上と正四位下は正四位に一本化。[[幕末]]の[[尊皇攘夷]]や[[明治維新]]において亡くなった功労者のうち、従三位以上に叙せられた[[元勲]]や[[公卿]]、[[大名]]などの[[華族]]を除いた、特に偉勲著しい者に対して正四位が[[贈位]]された。
政府においては正四位は[[事務次官]]、[[大日本帝国陸軍|大日本帝国陸]][[大日本帝国海軍|海軍]]では、[[大将]]の階級にある者の初叙位階とされた。その他、[[国会議員]]もその経歴・実績に応じ[[従一位]]から正四位の間で叙位される例が多い。
今日の栄典制度では、勲二等相当の功績ある人物が亡くなった際に叙位される。主な例としては国会議員や功績著しい大学教授（名誉教授の称号を与えられた者）にその例が見られる。また、学者、芸術家などで[[文化功労者]]に認められた者が死後に叙位されることが一般的である。

[[Category:Completion tier 2]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:Completion tier 3]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:Completion tier 3]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

[[Category:Court Ranks of Japan]][[Category:completion tier 4]] '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral, it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official)

It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-ranks/court-ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].

It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-ranks/court-ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]

In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]

'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-ranks/court-ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.

Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.

In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].

revision.text:
'''正四位'''（しょうしい）とは、[[日本]]の[[位階]]及び[[神階]]における位のひとつ。
[[従三位]]の下、[[従四位]]の上に位する。[[贈位]]の場合、贈正四位という。
== 概要 == ===官位相当制における正四位の位置付け=== 正四位は[[律令制]]下においては上下に分けられ、従三位の下、従四位の上に位する。[[勲等]]では、[[勲三等]]に相当し、[[官位相当]]では正四位上は[[中務省|中務卿]]、[[参議]]に相当し、正四位下は[[皇太子傅]]及び中務省を除く八省の[[長官]]である[[卿]]（[[式部省|式部卿]]、[[治部省|治部卿]]、[[民部省|民部卿]]、[[兵部省|兵部卿]]、[[刑部省|刑部卿]]、[[大蔵省 (律令制)|大蔵卿]]、[[宮内省 (律令制)|宮内卿]]）の職がこの位にあった。しかし、後代には正四位の位階は本来従三位相当である筈の[[近衛大将]]が大臣の兼官となることが慣例化するに連れて、従三位の者が[[近衛府|近衛中将]]に任ぜられ、三位中将となることが通例化すると、正四位の者は[[近衛府|近衛少将]]に任ぜられることが慣例化するようになった（[[結城秀康]]など）。但し、正四位上については従三位に昇進予定者が一時昇叙する特別な位階であり、[[官位相当制]]では正四位下が主に用いられた。尤も、江戸時代に入ると、[[彦根藩|彦根]][[藩主]]の[[井伊氏]]の極位が正四位上とされたこともあり、時代により位階の運用に差異があることは留意する必要がある。
=== 正四位の格式と主な叙位者 === 従四位同様、四位にある者の敬称は[[氏]]及び[[諱]]の下に、[[朝臣]]を付ける名乗りが基本である。例として「正四位下前[[伊予国|伊予守]][[源頼義]]朝臣」など。
しかし、正四位であっても[[参議]]となり、[[公卿]]に列した者への敬称は氏の下に「[[朝臣]]」、諱の下に「卿」と称した。 一方、正四位下は[[公卿]]に昇ることを許されない[[家柄]]の極位、即ち最高位であり、著名なところでは[[清和源氏]]とりわけ、[[摂津源氏]]、[[河内源氏]]の[[棟梁]]に多くみられた。[[清和源氏]]では初代 [[源経基|経基王]]その子の[[源満仲]]、また満仲の[[長男]] [[摂津源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼光]]、[[河内源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼義]]、[[源義家|義家]]親子など河内源氏代々の棟梁がその位階に昇った。また、[[摂津源氏]]の[[傍系]]ではある、[[美濃源氏]]の[[源光保]]は[[院近臣]]として活躍し、娘 [[土佐局]]が[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽法皇]]の寵妃となったことで正四位下に昇った。 一方、武家の棟梁として源氏と覇を競った[[平氏#桓武平氏|桓武平氏]]では、公家平氏を別として武家平氏については官位の面でも長らく源氏に遅れをとっていた。しかし、源義家の子 [[源義親|義親]]が[[九州]]や[[隠岐国]]で濫妨を働き、[[平正盛]]がこれを討伐したことで、平氏は家格を上昇させ、その子 [[平忠盛]]の代に正四位上[[刑部卿]]にまで昇り、その嫡男 [[平清盛|清盛]]も29歳の若さで正四位下中務大輔兼安芸守となり、[[平氏政権]]の礎を築いている。源氏においては、[[源頼朝|頼朝]]が平氏追討を遂げるまでの間、この位階に留まったほか、[[鎌倉時代]]は[[鎌倉幕府]][[執権]]北条氏の得宗及び有力一門や有が叙せられ、[[得宗]]では[[北条泰時]]が、有力一門では[[北条政村]]が叙せられた。そのほか、京都の学者貴族出身の有力御家人 [[大江広元]]もこの位階に叙せられている。
[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には飛騨の国司大名 [[姉小路氏]]や[[北畠氏]]が正四位ないし従三位に昇るなど公家大名に叙位例が見られる他、一国人領主ながら三管領斯波家の女を母とする、源氏の名門 [[村上義清]]が正四位上に昇っている。 [[江戸時代]]には、御三家の[[水戸藩]]の[[水戸徳川家]]の当主、家門大名では[[福井藩]]の[[越前松平家]]（15代中4人）、[[譜代大名]]では[[彦根藩]]の[[井伊氏]]（17代中3人）、[[外様大名]]の[[加賀藩]]の[[前田氏]]や[[薩摩藩]]の[[島津氏]]（12代中、[[島津斉宣]]のみ）、[[仙台藩]]の[[伊達氏]]（歴代では[[伊達慶邦]]のみ）などの大名家が昇ることを許された。
[[明治|明治時代]]以降、正四位上と正四位下は正四位に一本化。[[幕末]]の[[尊皇攘夷]]や[[明治維新]]において亡くなった功労者のうち、従三位以上に叙せられた[[元勲]]や[[公卿]]、[[大名]]などの[[華族]]を除いた、特に偉勲著しい者に対して正四位が[[贈位]]された。
政府においては正四位は[[事務次官]]、[[大日本帝国陸軍|大日本帝国陸]][[大日本帝国海軍|海軍]]では、[[大将]]の階級にある者の初叙位階とされた。その他、[[国会議員]]もその経歴・実績に応じ[[従一位]]から正四位の間で叙位される例が多い。
今日の栄典制度では、勲二等相当の功績ある人物が亡くなった際に叙位される。主な例としては国会議員や功績著しい大学教授（名誉教授の称号を与えられた者）にその例が見られる。また、学者、芸術家などで[[文化功労者]]に認められた者が死後に叙位されることが一般的である。

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Shinkai]] ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-ranks/court-ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==

Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].

'''正四位'''（しょうしい）とは、[[日本]]の[[位階]]及び[[神階]]における位のひとつ。
[[従三位]]の下、[[従四位]]の上に位する。[[贈位]]の場合、贈正四位という。
== 概要 == ===官位相当制における正四位の位置付け=== 正四位は[[律令制]]下においては上下に分けられ、従三位の下、従四位の上に位する。[[勲等]]では、[[勲三等]]に相当し、[[官位相当]]では正四位上は[[中務省|中務卿]]、[[参議]]に相当し、正四位下は[[皇太子傅]]及び中務省を除く八省の[[長官]]である[[卿]]（[[式部省|式部卿]]、[[治部省|治部卿]]、[[民部省|民部卿]]、[[兵部省|兵部卿]]、[[刑部省|刑部卿]]、[[大蔵省 (律令制)|大蔵卿]]、[[宮内省 (律令制)|宮内卿]]）の職がこの位にあった。しかし、後代には正四位の位階は本来従三位相当である筈の[[近衛大将]]が大臣の兼官となることが慣例化するに連れて、従三位の者が[[近衛府|近衛中将]]に任ぜられ、三位中将となることが通例化すると、正四位の者は[[近衛府|近衛少将]]に任ぜられることが慣例化するようになった（[[結城秀康]]など）。但し、正四位上については従三位に昇進予定者が一時昇叙する特別な位階であり、[[官位相当制]]では正四位下が主に用いられた。尤も、江戸時代に入ると、[[彦根藩|彦根]][[藩主]]の[[井伊氏]]の極位が正四位上とされたこともあり、時代により位階の運用に差異があることは留意する必要がある。
=== 正四位の格式と主な叙位者 === 従四位同様、四位にある者の敬称は[[氏]]及び[[諱]]の下に、[[朝臣]]を付ける名乗りが基本である。例として「正四位下前[[伊予国|伊予守]][[源頼義]]朝臣」など。
しかし、正四位であっても[[参議]]となり、[[公卿]]に列した者への敬称は氏の下に「[[朝臣]]」、諱の下に「卿」と称した。 一方、正四位下は[[公卿]]に昇ることを許されない[[家柄]]の極位、即ち最高位であり、著名なところでは[[清和源氏]]とりわけ、[[摂津源氏]]、[[河内源氏]]の[[棟梁]]に多くみられた。[[清和源氏]]では初代 [[源経基|経基王]]その子の[[源満仲]]、また満仲の[[長男]] [[摂津源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼光]]、[[河内源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼義]]、[[源義家|義家]]親子など河内源氏代々の棟梁がその位階に昇った。また、[[摂津源氏]]の[[傍系]]ではある、[[美濃源氏]]の[[源光保]]は[[院近臣]]として活躍し、娘 [[土佐局]]が[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽法皇]]の寵妃となったことで正四位下に昇った。 一方、武家の棟梁として源氏と覇を競った[[平氏#桓武平氏|桓武平氏]]では、公家平氏を別として武家平氏については官位の面でも長らく源氏に遅れをとっていた。しかし、源義家の子 [[源義親|義親]]が[[九州]]や[[隠岐国]]で濫妨を働き、[[平正盛]]がこれを討伐したことで、平氏は家格を上昇させ、その子 [[平忠盛]]の代に正四位上[[刑部卿]]にまで昇り、その嫡男 [[平清盛|清盛]]も29歳の若さで正四位下中務大輔兼安芸守となり、[[平氏政権]]の礎を築いている。源氏においては、[[源頼朝|頼朝]]が平氏追討を遂げるまでの間、この位階に留まったほか、[[鎌倉時代]]は[[鎌倉幕府]][[執権]]北条氏の得宗及び有力一門や有が叙せられ、[[得宗]]では[[北条泰時]]が、有力一門では[[北条政村]]が叙せられた。そのほか、京都の学者貴族出身の有力御家人 [[大江広元]]もこの位階に叙せられている。
[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には飛騨の国司大名 [[姉小路氏]]や[[北畠氏]]が正四位ないし従三位に昇るなど公家大名に叙位例が見られる他、一国人領主ながら三管領斯波家の女を母とする、源氏の名門 [[村上義清]]が正四位上に昇っている。 [[江戸時代]]には、御三家の[[水戸藩]]の[[水戸徳川家]]の当主、家門大名では[[福井藩]]の[[越前松平家]]（15代中4人）、[[譜代大名]]では[[彦根藩]]の[[井伊氏]]（17代中3人）、[[外様大名]]の[[加賀藩]]の[[前田氏]]や[[薩摩藩]]の[[島津氏]]（12代中、[[島津斉宣]]のみ）、[[仙台藩]]の[[伊達氏]]（歴代では[[伊達慶邦]]のみ）などの大名家が昇ることを許された。
[[明治|明治時代]]以降、正四位上と正四位下は正四位に一本化。[[幕末]]の[[尊皇攘夷]]や[[明治維新]]において亡くなった功労者のうち、従三位以上に叙せられた[[元勲]]や[[公卿]]、[[大名]]などの[[華族]]を除いた、特に偉勲著しい者に対して正四位が[[贈位]]された。
政府においては正四位は[[事務次官]]、[[大日本帝国陸軍|大日本帝国陸]][[大日本帝国海軍|海軍]]では、[[大将]]の階級にある者の初叙位階とされた。その他、[[国会議員]]もその経歴・実績に応じ[[従一位]]から正四位の間で叙位される例が多い。
今日の栄典制度では、勲二等相当の功績ある人物が亡くなった際に叙位される。主な例としては国会議員や功績著しい大学教授（名誉教授の称号を与えられた者）にその例が見られる。また、学者、芸術家などで[[文化功労者]]に認められた者が死後に叙位されることが一般的である。

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

'''正四位'''（しょうしい）とは、[[日本]]の[[位階]]及び[[神階]]における位のひとつ。
[[従三位]]の下、[[従四位]]の上に位する。[[贈位]]の場合、贈正四位という。
== 概要 == ===官位相当制における正四位の位置付け=== 正四位は[[律令制]]下においては上下に分けられ、従三位の下、従四位の上に位する。[[勲等]]では、[[勲三等]]に相当し、[[官位相当]]では正四位上は[[中務省|中務卿]]、[[参議]]に相当し、正四位下は[[皇太子傅]]及び中務省を除く八省の[[長官]]である[[卿]]（[[式部省|式部卿]]、[[治部省|治部卿]]、[[民部省|民部卿]]、[[兵部省|兵部卿]]、[[刑部省|刑部卿]]、[[大蔵省 (律令制)|大蔵卿]]、[[宮内省 (律令制)|宮内卿]]）の職がこの位にあった。しかし、後代には正四位の位階は本来従三位相当である筈の[[近衛大将]]が大臣の兼官となることが慣例化するに連れて、従三位の者が[[近衛府|近衛中将]]に任ぜられ、三位中将となることが通例化すると、正四位の者は[[近衛府|近衛少将]]に任ぜられることが慣例化するようになった（[[結城秀康]]など）。但し、正四位上については従三位に昇進予定者が一時昇叙する特別な位階であり、[[官位相当制]]では正四位下が主に用いられた。尤も、江戸時代に入ると、[[彦根藩|彦根]][[藩主]]の[[井伊氏]]の極位が正四位上とされたこともあり、時代により位階の運用に差異があることは留意する必要がある。
=== 正四位の格式と主な叙位者 === 従四位同様、四位にある者の敬称は[[氏]]及び[[諱]]の下に、[[朝臣]]を付ける名乗りが基本である。例として「正四位下前[[伊予国|伊予守]][[源頼義]]朝臣」など。
しかし、正四位であっても[[参議]]となり、[[公卿]]に列した者への敬称は氏の下に「[[朝臣]]」、諱の下に「卿」と称した。 一方、正四位下は[[公卿]]に昇ることを許されない[[家柄]]の極位、即ち最高位であり、著名なところでは[[清和源氏]]とりわけ、[[摂津源氏]]、[[河内源氏]]の[[棟梁]]に多くみられた。[[清和源氏]]では初代 [[源経基|経基王]]その子の[[源満仲]]、また満仲の[[長男]] [[摂津源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼光]]、[[河内源氏]]の棟梁 [[源頼義]]、[[源義家|義家]]親子など河内源氏代々の棟梁がその位階に昇った。また、[[摂津源氏]]の[[傍系]]ではある、[[美濃源氏]]の[[源光保]]は[[院近臣]]として活躍し、娘 [[土佐局]]が[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽法皇]]の寵妃となったことで正四位下に昇った。 一方、武家の棟梁として源氏と覇を競った[[平氏#桓武平氏|桓武平氏]]では、公家平氏を別として武家平氏については官位の面でも長らく源氏に遅れをとっていた。しかし、源義家の子 [[源義親|義親]]が[[九州]]や[[隠岐国]]で濫妨を働き、[[平正盛]]がこれを討伐したことで、平氏は家格を上昇させ、その子 [[平忠盛]]の代に正四位上[[刑部卿]]にまで昇り、その嫡男 [[平清盛|清盛]]も29歳の若さで正四位下中務大輔兼安芸守となり、[[平氏政権]]の礎を築いている。源氏においては、[[源頼朝|頼朝]]が平氏追討を遂げるまでの間、この位階に留まったほか、[[鎌倉時代]]は[[鎌倉幕府]][[執権]]北条氏の得宗及び有力一門や有が叙せられ、[[得宗]]では[[北条泰時]]が、有力一門では[[北条政村]]が叙せられた。そのほか、京都の学者貴族出身の有力御家人 [[大江広元]]もこの位階に叙せられている。
[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には飛騨の国司大名 [[姉小路氏]]や[[北畠氏]]が正四位ないし従三位に昇るなど公家大名に叙位例が見られる他、一国人領主ながら三管領斯波家の女を母とする、源氏の名門 [[村上義清]]が正四位上に昇っている。 [[江戸時代]]には、御三家の[[水戸藩]]の[[水戸徳川家]]の当主、家門大名では[[福井藩]]の[[越前松平家]]（15代中4人）、[[譜代大名]]では[[彦根藩]]の[[井伊氏]]（17代中3人）、[[外様大名]]の[[加賀藩]]の[[前田氏]]や[[薩摩藩]]の[[島津氏]]（12代中、[[島津斉宣]]のみ）、[[仙台藩]]の[[伊達氏]]（歴代では[[伊達慶邦]]のみ）などの大名家が昇ることを許された。
[[明治|明治時代]]以降、正四位上と正四位下は正四位に一本化。[[幕末]]の[[尊皇攘夷]]や[[明治維新]]において亡くなった功労者のうち、従三位以上に叙せられた[[元勲]]や[[公卿]]、[[大名]]などの[[華族]]を除いた、特に偉勲著しい者に対して正四位が[[贈位]]された。
政府においては正四位は[[事務次官]]、[[大日本帝国陸軍|大日本帝国陸]][[大日本帝国海軍|海軍]]では、[[大将]]の階級にある者の初叙位階とされた。その他、[[国会議員]]もその経歴・実績に応じ[[従一位]]から正四位の間で叙位される例が多い。
今日の栄典制度では、勲二等相当の功績ある人物が亡くなった際に叙位される。主な例としては国会議員や功績著しい大学教授（名誉教授の称号を与えられた者）にその例が見られる。また、学者、芸術家などで[[文化功労者]]に認められた者が死後に叙位されることが一般的である。

'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *
