revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[Ōkura-shō|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.comment: Bot: convert local link → enwiki interwiki
revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[Gyōbu-shō|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].

In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===

The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].

* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]

revision.comment: Bot: convert local link → enwiki interwiki
revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[Meiji period]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.comment: Bot: convert local link → enwiki interwiki
revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[Nakatsukasa-shō]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[Sangi]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].

In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].

== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==

revision.comment: Text replacement - "Greater Initial Rank" to "Senior Initial Rank"
revision.text:
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].

revision.text:
<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].

It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

revision.comment: Bot: add interwikis from Wikidata
revision.text:
<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]] (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]] (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11123338]] Wikidata name: Senior Fourth Rank [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of [[:en:Japan|Japan]] and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of [[:en:Order of Merit|Order of Merit]], it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as [[:en:Chūnagon|Chūnagon]] and [[:en:Sangi (Japan)|Sangi (Japan)]], while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]], such as the [[:en:Shikibu-shō|Shikibu-kyō]], [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|Gyōbu-kyō]], [[:en:Ministry of the Treasury|Ōkura-kyō]], and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the [[:en:Ii clan|Ii clan]] of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the [[:en:Seiwa Genji|Seiwa Genji]], such as [[:en:Minamoto no Mitsunaka|Minamoto no Mitsunaka]] and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the [[:en:Heike|Heike]], also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]] and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to [[:en:Order of Culture|Second Order of Merit]] in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], [[:en:Natsume Sōseki|Natsume Sōseki]], and [[:en:Kōichi Kido|Kōichi Kido]].
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:正四位]][[ko:정4위]][[zh:正四位]]
'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}} and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of {{ill|Order of Merit|en|Order of Merit|WD=Q94056|lt=Order of Merit}}, it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as {{ill|Chūnagon|en|Chūnagon|WD=Q1185382|lt=Chūnagon}} and {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|WD=Q1133663|lt=Sangi (Japan)}}, while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}}, such as the {{ill|Shikibu-shō|en|Shikibu-shō|WD=Q3727885|lt=Shikibu-kyō}}, [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], {{ill|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|en|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|WD=Q6867320|lt=Gyōbu-kyō}}, {{ill|Ministry of the Treasury|en|Ministry of the Treasury|WD=Q112323848|lt=Ōkura-kyō}}, and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the {{ill|Ii clan|en|Ii clan|WD=Q2243336|lt=Ii clan}} of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the {{ill|Seiwa Genji|en|Seiwa Genji|WD=Q2164991|lt=Seiwa Genji}}, such as {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|WD=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the {{ill|Heike|en|Heike|WD=Q5699231|lt=Heike}}, also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to {{ill|Order of Culture|en|Order of Culture|WD=Q530124|lt=Second Order of Merit}} in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|WD=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki}}, and {{ill|Kōichi Kido|en|Kōichi Kido|WD=Q699712|lt=Kōichi Kido}}.
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|WD=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * {{ill|Kido Takayoshi|en|Kido Takayoshi|WD=Q696402|lt=Kido Takayoshi}} * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|WD=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki}} (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * {{ill|Kōichi Kido|en|Kōichi Kido|WD=Q699712|lt=Kōichi Kido}} (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *

In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of {{ill|Order of Merit|en|Order of Merit|WD=Q94056|lt=Order of Merit|1=Order of Merit}}, it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as {{ill|Chūnagon|en|Chūnagon|WD=Q1185382|lt=Chūnagon|1=Chūnagon}} and {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|WD=Q1133663|lt=Sangi (Japan)|1=Sangi (Japan)}}, while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center}}, such as the {{ill|Shikibu-shō|en|Shikibu-shō|WD=Q3727885|lt=Shikibu-kyō|1=Shikibu-shō}}, [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], {{ill|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|en|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|WD=Q6867320|lt=Gyōbu-kyō|1=Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)}}, {{ill|Ministry of the Treasury|en|Ministry of the Treasury|WD=Q112323848|lt=Ōkura-kyō|1=Ministry of the Treasury}}, and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the {{ill|Ii clan|en|Ii clan|WD=Q2243336|lt=Ii clan|1=Ii clan}} of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the {{ill|Seiwa Genji|en|Seiwa Genji|WD=Q2164991|lt=Seiwa Genji|1=Seiwa Genji}}, such as {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|WD=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka|1=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the {{ill|Heike|en|Heike|WD=Q5699231|lt=Heike|1=Heike}}, also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to {{ill|Order of Culture|en|Order of Culture|WD=Q530124|lt=Second Order of Merit|1=Order of Culture}} in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|WD=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki|1=Natsume Sōseki}}, and {{ill|Kōichi Kido|en|Kōichi Kido|WD=Q699712|lt=Kōichi Kido|1=Kōichi Kido}}.
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|WD=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka|1=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * {{ill|Kido Takayoshi|en|Kido Takayoshi|WD=Q696402|lt=Kido Takayoshi|1=Kido Takayoshi}} * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==

'''Shōshii''' (正四位) is one of the Ranks in the [[Ritsuryō system]] of {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}} and its corresponding [[Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]] Ranks.
It is positioned below {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|1=Junior Third Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Third Rank|qq=}} and above {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位|1=Junior Fourth Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}}. In the case of a posthumous conferral,<ref>https://www.wakapoetry.net/background/society/court-offices-titles-and-Ranks/court-Ranks/</ref> it is referred to as "Zōshōshii."
== Overview ==
=== Position of Shōshii in the Ritsuryō System ===
In the [[Ritsuryō system]], Shōshii was divided into upper and lower Ranks, positioned below Jusanmi and above Jushii. In terms of {{ill|Order of Merit|en|Order of Merit|qid=Q94056|lt=Order of Merit|1=Order of Merit}}, it corresponded to the [[Third Order of Merit]]. The [[Kan'i Correspondence]] assigned Shōshii Upper to positions such as {{ill|Chūnagon|en|Chūnagon|qid=Q1185382|lt=Chūnagon|1=Chūnagon}} and {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|qid=Q1133663|lt=Sangi (Japan)|1=Sangi (Japan)}}, while Shōshii Lower was equivalent to the heads of the [[Eight Ministries]] excluding the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|qid=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center|1=Ministry of the Center}}, such as the {{ill|Shikibu-shō|en|Shikibu-shō|qid=Q3727885|lt=Shikibu-kyō|1=Shikibu-shō}}, [[:en:Jibu-shō|Jibu-kyō]], [[:en:Minbu-shō|Minbu-kyō]], [[:en:Hyōbu-shō|Hyōbu-kyō]], {{ill|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|en|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|qid=Q6867320|lt=Gyōbu-kyō|1=Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)}}, {{ill|Ministry of the Treasury|en|Ministry of the Treasury|qid=Q112323848|lt=Ōkura-kyō|1=Ministry of the Treasury}}, and [[:en:Kunai-shō|Kunai-kyō]].
However, in later periods, Shōshii was often associated with those who held the title of [[Konoefu|Konoefu commanders]]. It became customary for individuals promoted to Shōshii Upper to eventually rise to Jusanmi. Meanwhile, Shōshii Lower primarily denoted positions such as [[Konoefu|Konoefu vice-commanders]], emphasizing a transitional Rank.
In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the Rank of Shōshii Upper was designated as the highest Rank for certain domains, such as the {{ill|Ii clan|en|Ii clan|qid=Q2243336|lt=Ii clan|1=Ii clan}} of [[Hikone domain]], reflecting varied practices across historical periods.
=== Honorifics and Key Figures Elevated to Shōshii ===
Like Jushii, individuals holding Shōshii were referred to with the honorific [[Ason]] appended to their names. For instance, "Shōshii no Ge, Former [[Governor of Iyo Province]] [[Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Yoriyoshi Ason]]."
Prominent examples of individuals elevated to this Rank include the heads of the {{ill|Seiwa Genji|en|Seiwa Genji|qid=Q2164991|lt=Seiwa Genji|1=Seiwa Genji}}, such as {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|qid=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka|1=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} and his descendants, including [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who later achieved [[Senior Third Rank|Juni'i]]. Notable figures in other military clans, like [[Taira no Kiyomori]] of the {{ill|Heike|en|Heike|qid=Q5699231|lt=Heike|1=Heike}}, also attained Shōshii as their clans rose to prominence.
== Modern Recognition and Posthumous Conferral ==
In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} and beyond, Shōshii Upper and Lower were unified into a single Rank of Shōshii. It became a prestigious posthumous honor granted to individuals of exceptional merit, including [[Meiji Restoration]] figures and cultural contributors. The Rank is equivalent to {{ill|Order of Culture|en|Order of Culture|qid=Q530124|lt=Second Order of Merit|1=Order of Culture}} in modern Japan's [[honors system]].
Prominent examples include [[:en:scholars|scholars]], [[:en:Artists|Artists]], and [[:en:Government officials|Government officials]]. Individuals posthumously awarded Shōshii include [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]], {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|qid=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki|1=Natsume Sōseki}}, and {{ill|Kōichi Kido|en|Kōichi Kido|qid=Q699712|lt=Kōichi Kido|1=Kōichi Kido}}.
== Figures Historically Awarded Shōshii ==
* {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|en|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|qid=Q2531241|lt=Minamoto no Mitsunaka|1=Minamoto no Mitsunaka}} * [[Taira no Kiyomori]] * [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] * {{ill|Kido Takayoshi|en|Kido Takayoshi|qid=Q696402|lt=Kido Takayoshi|1=Kido Takayoshi}} * [[Itō Hirobumi]]
== Modern Posthumous Recipients of Shōshii ==
* {{ill|Natsume Sōseki|en|Natsume Sōseki|qid=Q180903|lt=Natsume Sōseki|1=Natsume Sōseki}} (novelist) * [[:en:Akinari Ueda|Akinari Ueda]] (scholar) * {{ill|Kōichi Kido|en|Kōichi Kido|qid=Q699712|lt=Kōichi Kido|1=Kōichi Kido}} (official) {{Court Ranks of Japan}} *
